description: Part 1 (metrics + logs): the full base lab. FastAPI API in app/ with Prometheus instrumentation, structured JSON logging, and OTel client wiring (trace_id present/empty); node_exporter, Prometheus, Loki, Grafana Alloy, and Grafana (datasources + provider + two dashboards) all wired in docker-compose.yml on internal network obsnet; pytest tests; and the load-test script. This feature leaves a working metrics+logs stack. It is the foundation FEAT-002 extends (service-b, collector, Jaeger). Independent of FEAT-003 (docs) except that FEAT-003 documents it.
steps: Create repo scaffolding: .gitignore (ignore .env, __pycache__, *.pyc, loki/grafana data dirs), .env.example (GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD placeholder, LOAD_TEST_RATE/DURATION, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317), README.md pointing to the two tutorials. No real secrets.

Create app/ FastAPI API (app/main.py) with endpoints: GET /health, GET /, GET /products, GET /products/{id} (404 when id missing from the in-memory product list), GET /simulate-error (controlled 500; return 400 when a bad query param is supplied), GET /simulate-slow (bounded artificial latency from a capped ?seconds query, default small). Returns 200/400/404/500 reproducibly.

app/metrics.py: prometheus-client instrumentation — Counter for total requests, requests per normalized route template (NOT raw dynamic path), per HTTP status class (2xx/4xx/5xx); Histogram for request latency with buckets enabling histogram_quantile p50/p90/p99; a Gauge for API up. Expose GET /metrics. Middleware labels requests with request.scope route template to avoid high-cardinality labels (no user ids, IPs, request ids, raw dynamic segments).

app/logging_config.py: structured JSON logging to stdout with timestamp, severity, http method, normalized route, status code, request duration (ms), correlation id (generate/propagate an X-Correlation-ID header), error message when present, and trace_id (from the current OTel span context, empty string when no active trace). Never log secrets/tokens/passwords.

app/otel.py: OTel SDK 1.27.0 setup — TracerProvider with resource service.name=obs-lab-api, OTLP span exporter to env OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, BatchSpanProcessor; instrument FastAPI and httpx (auto-instrumentation 0.48b0). Guard with an env flag so it is a no-op when the collector is absent (keeps Part 1 runnable standalone).

app/requirements.txt pinned: fastapi==0.115.*, uvicorn==0.32.*, prometheus-client==0.21.*, opentelemetry-sdk==1.27.0, opentelemetry-exporter-otlp==1.27.0, opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi==0.48b0, opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx==0.48b0, httpx. app/Dockerfile: python:3.12-slim, install reqs, run uvicorn app.main:app on 0.0.0.0:8000.

config/prometheus/prometheus.yml: scrape_configs for node_exporter:9100, api:8000/metrics, service-b:8001/metrics (target may be down until FEAT-002), and prometheus itself. Reasonable scrape_interval.
config/loki/loki-config.yml: single-binary Loki 3.1, filesystem storage, no auth, sane retention for a lab.

config/alloy/config.alloy: discover docker container logs for api and service-b, parse, and push to Loki at http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push with labels (container/service). Mount docker socket read-only.

config/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml: Prometheus (default), Loki with derivedFields extracting trace_id via regex and linking to the Jaeger datasource uid, and Jaeger datasource with tracesToLogsV2 pointing at the Loki datasource. config/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/dashboards.yml: a file provider pointing at /var/lib/grafana/dashboards.

config/grafana/dashboards/infra.json: node_exporter OS metrics dashboard — CPU usage, memory used/available, disk usage, network activity, exporter up, scrape health; with titles, units, legends, refresh interval, and panel descriptions; include text clearly stating these are node_exporter OS metrics, NOT CloudWatch.

config/grafana/dashboards/api.json: API dashboard — total requests, requests per endpoint, per status, 2xx/4xx/5xx counts, error rate, latency p50/p90/p99 via histogram_quantile over the histogram buckets, requests/sec, API health; with titles/units/legends/refresh/descriptions.

docker-compose.yml: single network obsnet (bridge, internal wiring). Services with pinned image tags: api (build app/, publish 8000), service-b (build service-b/ — may be fully defined in FEAT-002; include a placeholder service entry OR leave to FEAT-002 and note the dependency), node_exporter prom/node-exporter:v1.8.*, prometheus prom/prometheus:v2.54.*, loki grafana/loki:3.1.*, alloy grafana/alloy:v1.3.*, grafana grafana/grafana:11.2.* (publish 3000, env admin password from .env). Only grafana and api publish host ports; others internal-only. NOTE: otel-collector and jaeger are added in FEAT-002.

scripts/load_test.py: generate mixed traffic (success, 404, 500, slow) against the API for a configurable duration and rate with safe defaults rate-limited for t3.small (e.g. a few req/s). Use httpx; argparse for --duration and --rate.

tests/__init__.py and tests/test_api.py: pytest + FastAPI TestClient covering 200 (/, /products), 404 (missing product), 500 (/simulate-error), 400 (bad query), and the /simulate-slow endpoint (assert it responds within the capped bound). No tests beyond lab verification.
acceptance_criteria: `docker compose config` is valid and `docker compose build` builds the api image.
`docker compose up -d` starts api, node_exporter, prometheus, loki, alloy, grafana; `docker compose ps` shows them running/healthy.
curl http://localhost:8000/metrics returns Prometheus metrics with normalized-route labels and latency histogram buckets.
Prometheus has node_exporter, api, and prometheus targets up; Grafana datasources load green and both dashboards appear.
Running scripts/load_test.py changes the API dashboard graphs; API logs are JSON and queryable in Loki via Grafana.
verification: python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r app/requirements.txt pytest && pytest tests/
docker compose up -d && docker compose ps
python scripts/load_test.py --duration 30 --rate 3 (then confirm in Grafana manually)
findings:
IMPLEMENTED & VERIFIED (committed on branch main, commit 'feat: part 1 metrics+logs...').

VERIFICATION RESULTS (local Docker Desktop on macOS):
- `docker compose config`: valid. `docker compose build api`: builds image obs-lab-api:1.0.0.
- `pytest tests/`: 12 passed (200/400/404/500/slow-bound/422-over-cap/metrics/correlation-id).
- `docker compose up -d`: api, node_exporter, prometheus, loki, alloy, grafana all Up.
- Prometheus targets api, node_exporter, prometheus are UP; service-b DOWN as expected (FEAT-002).
- /metrics exposes normalized-route labels (e.g. route="/products/{product_id}") and api_request_duration_seconds_bucket; /metrics scrape is excluded from its own counters.
- Grafana: datasources Prometheus(default)/Loki/Jaeger provisioned; Prometheus+Loki health green; both dashboards (uids obs-lab-infra, obs-lab-api) auto-loaded. Jaeger health N/A until FEAT-002.
- load_test.py generated mixed 200/400/404/500 traffic; status-class counters moved; Alloy shipped JSON logs to Loki queryable as {service="obs-lab-api"}.

COULD NOT RUN on this host (macOS Docker Desktop limitations, NOT code defects):
- Host port 8000 was occupied by an unrelated java process, so api was verified on an alternate published host port (18000) via a throwaway compose override; the committed docker-compose.yml keeps api on 8000 (correct for EC2).
- node_exporter: removed the `rslave` bind-propagation flag from the `/:/host` mount because Docker Desktop rejects it ('path / is mounted on / but it is not a shared or slave mount'). Plain `:ro` works on both macOS and Amazon Linux 2023. node_exporter target then reported UP.

=== HANDOFF FOR FEAT-002 ===
- Network: single bridge network `obsnet` (compose project name 'challenge-sre' -> actual net 'challenge-sre_obsnet'). Add service-b, otel-collector, jaeger to this same network.
- Container names (used by Alloy log discovery regex): api=`obs-lab-api`, and service-b MUST be named `obs-lab-service-b` so config/alloy/config.alloy keeps/labels it (regex keeps '/(obs-lab-api|obs-lab-service-b)', sets labels container & service). Add any new service to that regex if you want its logs in Loki.
- Ports: only grafana(3000) and api(8000) publish host ports; everything else internal-only. service-b listens on 8001 (Prometheus already scrapes service-b:8001/metrics; job 'service-b' is pre-added in config/prometheus/prometheus.yml). Jaeger UI expected at jaeger:16686 (datasource already points there). OTel collector endpoint expected at otel-collector:4317 (gRPC).
- OTel gating: app/otel.py setup_otel(app) is a NO-OP unless env OTEL_ENABLED is truthy (1/true/yes/on). Enable it by setting OTEL_ENABLED=true on the api (and service-b) service env in Part 2; OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT defaults to http://otel-collector:4317 (gRPC, insecure). app also auto-instruments httpx, so outbound calls api->service-b propagate W3C traceparent automatically. current_trace_id() returns 32-hex trace id or '' when no active trace.
- trace_id log field: the structured JSON log field name is exactly `trace_id` (lowercase). The X-Correlation-ID header field logs as `correlation_id`.
- Grafana datasource UIDs (stable, in config/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml): prometheus=`prometheus` (default), loki=`loki`, jaeger=`jaeger`. Loki derivedFields regex extracts trace_id via '"trace_id"\s*:\s*"([a-f0-9]+)"' and links to datasourceUid `jaeger`. Jaeger tracesToLogsV2 points back to datasourceUid `loki` (tag key service.name -> value label 'service'). The Jaeger SERVICE itself still needs to be created in FEAT-002 (datasource is pre-provisioned).
- Reminders from context.json for FEAT-002: Jaeger all-in-one needs env COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true to accept OTLP on 4317/4318; OTel Collector contrib 0.109 has NO jaeger exporter — use the `otlp` exporter to jaeger:4317. Pin Jaeger 1.60, OTel Collector contrib 0.109.
- Image/volume naming: api image tag obs-lab-api:1.0.0; named volumes prometheus_data/loki_data/grafana_data. Grafana admin password from .env GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD (default 'admin' if unset).
